noPlan.decisiveGap: No discovered opening has an established fulfiller, full direct cost, price or close rate that fits $3,000 settled in 21 days inside $300 and 6 owner hours. Brain holds no proved deliverable, so every build is subcontracted; the going bid for a comparable small-business site is ~$366 plus the employer fee. After Stripe fees (2.9% + 30c) 3 orders at $1,000 settle only ~$2,912, so 4 are needed; with $47 Instantly and up to $19 for a sending mailbox, $234 is left, so four builds must each cost <= $56 including the 3% employer fee - because Stripe holds the first payout 7-14 days, buyer money cannot fund them. No record shows a cold-reached local business paying $1,000 (Freelancer budgets and the Clutch figure were rejected as buyer-paid prices), and no paid rate is measured.
noPlan.resolution: A <= $66 experiment that is the whole plan if it passes. Day 1: owner posts the spec on Freelancer.com (free) for fixed quotes <= $56 all-in, opens Instantly Growth ($47, warm-up included) with his existing mailbox or a ~$19 new one, and spends at most 1 h compiling 200 local businesses with public emails. Day 3, only if a quote <= $56 from a developer with a verifiable portfolio exists: send a $1,000 offer paid 100% up front to the 200 contacts at ~40/day. PROOF by day 7: 4 paid $1,000 orders (2% of 200) - the paid orders are the price evidence. If it passes: $4,000 taken by day 7 settles by day 21 (14-day first payout), less ~$119 Stripe fees = ~$3,881 settled; spend $66 + 4 x $56 = $290 <= $300; owner hours 0.5 + 0.5 + 1 + 1.5 + 4 x 0.5 = 5.5 <= 6. STOP: no quote <= $56 by day 3 - send nothing, loss <= $66. Fewer than 4 paid orders by day 7 - $3,000 cannot settle by day 21; deliver the orders taken (each build <= $56 stays inside $300) and stop. A 2% paid rate from 200 cold emails is far above any measured reply benchmark, so the owner should expect the stop: the gap closes only with more spend or more weeks, which no established figure yet sizes.

answers.resolution: Accepted: t2 now budgets $47 Instantly plus up to $19 for a domain + mailbox (estimate; $0 if the owner connects an existing mailbox). A fresh mailbox sends only ~40/day, so the test reach is cut to 200 contacts over days 3-7, and the deliverability risk is stated.
Accepted: the build ceiling is now <= $56 per build all-in including the 3% employer fee.
Accepted: t3 is an OWNER step - compile 200 businesses with public emails from map/directory listings, hours unknown and capped at 1 h; if fewer are found the test runs on those.
Accepted: members hold only cop_88419; cop_9026 moved to excluded with its arithmetic.

answers.resolution: Accepted: 3 orders settle ~$2,912, so the proof is now 4 paid orders by day 7 (~$3,881 settled after fees); spend $66 + 4 x $56 = $290; owner hours 5.5 of 6.
No EVIDENCE fact states the full direct cost; ECONOMICS stays a decisive missing link, and every cost the test needs (Instantly, mailbox, all-in build fee) is now in the ledger or the ceiling.

noPlan.decisiveGap: No discovered opening has an established fulfiller, full direct cost, price or close rate that fits $3,000 settled in 21 days inside $300 and 6 owner hours. Brain holds no proved deliverable, so every build is subcontracted; the going bid for a comparable small-business site is ~$366 plus the employer fee. After Stripe fees (2.9% + 30c) 3 orders at $1,000 settle only ~$2,912, so 4 are needed; with $47 Instantly and up to $19 for a sending mailbox, $234 is left, so four builds must each cost <= $56 including the 3% employer fee - because Stripe holds the first payout 7-14 days, buyer money cannot fund them. No record shows a cold-reached local business paying $1,000 (Freelancer budgets and the Clutch figure were rejected as buyer-paid prices), and no paid rate is measured.
noPlan.resolution: A <= $66 experiment that is the whole plan if it passes. Day 1: owner posts the spec on Freelancer.com (free) for fixed quotes <= $56 all-in, opens Instantly Growth ($47, warm-up included) with his existing mailbox or a ~$19 new one, and spends at most 1 h compiling 200 local businesses with public emails. Day 3, only if a quote <= $56 from a developer with a verifiable portfolio exists: send a $1,000 offer paid 100% up front to the 200 contacts at ~40/day. PROOF by day 7: 4 paid $1,000 orders (2% of 200) - the paid orders are the price evidence. If it passes: $4,000 taken by day 7 settles by day 21 (14-day first payout), less ~$119 Stripe fees = ~$3,881 settled; spend $66 + 4 x $56 = $290 <= $300; owner hours 0.5 + 0.5 + 1 + 1.5 + 4 x 0.5 = 5.5 <= 6. STOP: no quote <= $56 by day 3 - send nothing, loss <= $66. Fewer than 4 paid orders by day 7 - $3,000 cannot settle by day 21; deliver the orders taken (each build <= $56 stays inside $300) and stop. A 2% paid rate from 200 cold emails is far above any measured reply benchmark, so the owner should expect the stop: the gap closes only with more spend or more weeks, which no established figure yet sizes.
